options.definition: a test replaces the code under test with a double, so it passes while the code is wrong
doubles stand only at the boundary; the unit under test runs for real

examples: a test that stubs the function it claims to verify, then asserts the stub ran
not_for: doubles at the system boundary, such as a fake clock

options.definition: a test writes to a live or shared system
tests run against sandbox doubles with no outside connection

examples: a test creating rows in the shared development database
not_for: read-only fixtures committed with the repository

options.definition: a test can pass without checking anything: no assertion, or one that cannot fail
each test asserts an outcome that the pre-fix code fails

examples: a test that calls the function and asserts true
not_for: smoke tests that fail loudly on exceptions

options.definition: a test asserts its doubles were called instead of asserting an outcome
assertions read outcomes; doubles are setup, not the subject

examples: asserting the sender mock received exactly one call, with no check on what was sent
not_for: contract tests whose subject is the call itself

options.definition: a test waits on real time: sleeping, polling a clock, or racing a timeout
timing comes from a fake clock or an explicit signal

examples: sleeping two seconds then hoping the worker finished
not_for: performance tests measuring real elapsed time

options.definition: a test's result depends on the machine: environment, locale, or files outside the repo
the test sets its world up itself and passes on any machine

examples: skipping unless an environment variable names a real account

options.definition: tests share writable state: files, rows, or globals one test leaves for the next
each test builds and tears down its own state

examples: two tests writing the same fixture file in the repository

options.definition: a test hides errors it should surface: broad catches that pass anyway
errors fail the test unless the test names the exact error it expects

examples: wrapping the call in a bare except that records nothing
not_for: tests of the error path itself

options.definition: a test pins implementation details: privates, call counts, or internal order
assertions read public behavior only

examples: asserting a private helper ran three times
not_for: white-box tests whose subject is the internals

options.definition: two tests assert the same behavior, so one can rot while the other guards it
each behavior has one test that guards it

examples: a new test repeating the assertions of the test beside it

options.definition: a test bakes in the current date, time, or data that will rot
dates and data come from fixed fixtures or a fake clock

examples: asserting an expiry computed from the real current year
not_for: tests of time handling with a fake clock

options.definition: a test uses randomness no seed fixes, so failures cannot repeat
each random choice takes a fixed seed

examples: generating ids with no seed, then asserting on their order
not_for: fuzzing harnesses, which log their seeds
